draft.title: New political ideas
card: the belief that every person has basic freedoms that a ruler cannot simply take away, such as freedom of speech.
the belief that ordinary people should have a say in government, usually by voting for their leaders.
the belief that people who share a language, history or culture should form their own nation and have pride in it.
the belief that wealth and major industries should be shared more equally or owned by the community, because workers made little from factory work.
draft.remember: After the American and French revolutions, these ideas changed how people thought they should be governed.

a.q: A group of people who share a language and history demand their own independent country. Which idea are they acting on?
a.why: Nationalism is the belief that people with a shared language, history or culture should form their own nation. Democracy is tempting, but it is about people having a say in government, not about forming a nation.
a.clue: Think about what the group shares and what it wants to form.

b.q: In 1850, a factory worker in a British town argues that the owners keep most of the wealth while workers stay poor, and that industries should be shared more equally. Which idea is this?
b.why: The worker wants wealth shared more equally, which is socialism. Democracy is tempting because it is about ordinary people, but it concerns having a say in government through voting, not how wealth is shared.
b.clue: Focus on what the worker wants to change: government, nation or wealth?
